title: Separate assets for cost-base adjustment
full_text:
An SMSF technical expert has highlighted the need for funds with investments held through a wrap account to disaggregate their details as soon as possible if they wish to apply the Division 296 cost-base adjustment to those assets.
Heffron head of SMSF technical and education services Lyn Formica said funds in this circumstance will have those investments recorded in financial statements as a single line item and had until lodgement of the 2027 annual return to elect to use the cost-base adjustment, but had to decide when to separately identify the assets for that purpose.
“If we want to put them back into their individual assets within the financial statements, do we do that at 30 June 2026, before the 2026 return is lodged, so we can use the cost-base adjustment or do we do it as part of the 2027 financials?” Formica said during an online update yesterday.
“Generally speaking, we are doing it as part of the 2026 financials. The reason for that is if we have a fund that’s going to opt into the cost-base adjustment, we need to be able to record the cost bases at 30 June 2026 of all of those individual assets.
“We want to be able to rely upon our software to produce the minutes that record that we have made the election and these were all of the assets that were owned by the fund on 30 June 2026, and this was the market value of those assets at that particular point in time.
“That’s going to be easier if we’ve already disaggregated them in the 2026 accounts.
“If you are not worried about that, then perhaps you could do it in 2027, but have a think about how much data you get from the wrap account, whether the SMSF is buying and selling assets in 2027 and if you are happy manually tracking the cost bases.
“In some cases, we’re actually not just ‘unblobbing’ the assets in 2026, we are doing it at 1 July 2025 because we want to be sure we have all the individual assets recorded throughout the 2026 year so we can get the right 12-month discount records happening for each of those underlying assets if we know we are not able to rely upon the wrap account’s records for that.”
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation and Investments
